rows.title: Planning as Inference: the EFE Policy-Selection Bridge

maturity_record.invariant: On a finite policy carrier with fixed precision, the KL-regularized control objective (expected EFE plus inverse-precision KL to the prior) is minimized exactly by the Boltzmann control posterior proportional to prior * exp(-gamma * G); the minimized value is -gamma^-1 log Z, the EFE splits as risk plus ambiguity, and the finite and treewise argmin views agree.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The bridge is a finite-carrier Gibbs/Donsker-Varadhan statement about the EFE control objective; it is not a general planning algorithm or a continuous-action result, and the policy-tree agreement is restricted to the treewise value surface of the policy_tree module.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The finite argmin exists and attains the closed-form Boltzmann value -gamma^-1 log Z for nonempty policy sets.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of all nine fep-156 declarations.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep156_boltzmann_control_posterior_minim:
theorem fep156_boltzmann_control_posterior_minimizes_efe (prior : FiniteLaw Action)
    (prior_pos : ∀ policy, 0 < prior policy) (γ : ℝ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (cost : Action → ℝ) (Q : FiniteLaw Action) :
    efeControlObjective prior γ cost (controlPosterior prior γ cost) ≤
      efeControlObjective prior γ cost Q ∧
    (efeControlObjective prior γ cost Q =
        efeControlObjective prior γ cost (controlPosterior prior γ cost) ↔
      Q = controlPosterior prior γ cost)

theorem fep156_boltzmann_control_posterior_minimal_value (prior : FiniteLaw Action)
    (prior_pos : ∀ policy, 0 < prior policy) (γ : ℝ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (cost : Action → ℝ) :
    efeControlObjective prior γ cost (controlPosterior prior γ cost) =
      -(γ⁻¹ * Real.log (efeControlPartition prior γ cost))
qualified_declaration_statements.fep156_efeControlObjective_eq_gibbsFreeE:
theorem fep156_efeControlObjective_eq_gibbsFreeEnergy (prior : FiniteLaw Action)
    (prior_pos : ∀ policy, 0 < prior policy) (γ : ℝ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (cost : Action → ℝ) (Q : FiniteLaw Action) :
    efeControlObjective prior γ cost Q =
      γ⁻¹ * gibbsFreeEnergy (efeGibbsCertificate prior prior_pos γ cost) Q
qualified_declaration_statements.fep156_efeControlObjective_eq_kl_sub_log:
theorem fep156_efeControlObjective_eq_kl_sub_logPartition (prior : FiniteLaw Action)
    (prior_pos : ∀ policy, 0 < prior policy) (γ : ℝ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (cost : Action → ℝ) (Q : FiniteLaw Action) :
    efeControlObjective prior γ cost Q =
      γ⁻¹ * (finiteKL Q (controlPosterior prior γ cost) -
        Real.log (efeControlPartition prior γ cost))
qualified_declaration_statements.fep156_efeControlObjective_sub_eq_kl:
theorem fep156_efeControlObjective_sub_eq_kl (prior : FiniteLaw Action)
    (prior_pos : ∀ policy, 0 < prior policy) (γ : ℝ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (cost : Action → ℝ) (Q : FiniteLaw Action) :
    efeControlObjective prior γ cost Q -
        efeControlObjective prior γ cost (controlPosterior prior γ cost) =
      γ⁻¹ * finiteKL Q (controlPosterior prior γ cost)

qualified_declaration_statements.fep156_policyTree_value_agreement:

    (model : EFEPolicyTreeModel Belief State Action Observation)
    (depth : ℕ) (belief : Belief) :
    policyTreeValue (riskAmbiguityPolicyTreeModel model)
        (optimalPolicyTree (efePolicyTreeModel model) depth belief) belief =
      optimalTreeValue (riskAmbiguityPolicyTreeModel model) depth belief ∧
    policyTreeValue (efePolicyTreeModel model)
        (optimalPolicyTree (riskAmbiguityPolicyTreeModel model) depth belief)

      optimalTreeValue (efePolicyTreeModel model) depth belief

rows.statement_review: For full-support finite prior and precision gamma>0, the Boltzmann law is the unique minimizer over probability laws of expected supplied cost plus KL(Q||prior)/gamma; optimum value is-logZ/gamma. Separate declarations establish deterministic EFE argmin/risk+ambiguity agreement and finite tree value agreement.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The main cost is an arbitrary real function, not automatically derived EFE. Deterministic finiteArgmin of EFE is not the Boltzmann probability law and does not attain the same KL-regularized objective value. The owner already has supported sparse-prior extensions, negative-precision maximum and zero/unsupported controls; released row is the full-support positive-precision case.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Uniform two-policy prior with costs0,1 and gamma1 gives a nondegenerate Boltzmann law; compare its regularized optimum-log((1+exp(-1))/2) with deterministic zero-cost selection penaltylog2.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Negative precision reverses divided-objective optimization and unsupported candidates can exploit totalized KL; actual source controls already show these boundaries. Zero precision removes the KL penalty and does not have the same unique minimum reading.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 008 deterministic finite minimization,028 normalized softmax and059 Gibbs/DV objective are distinct operations linked here under explicit premises;133 tree agreement remains finite/model-derived.

novelty_record.new_invariant: For fixed positive precision the Boltzmann control posterior minimizes the KL-regularized expected-cost objective over every normalized candidate law and is its unique minimizer.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds an explicit finite policy prior, precision, and cost field so the truncated EFE convention's argmin content becomes an attained finite Gibbs optimizer with closed-form negative log-partition value.

touching_relations.rationale: The exact Boltzmann-form control posterior minimizes the expected free energy with its uniqueness certificate, paired with fep-021's truncated-EFE epistemic-plus-pragmatic balance as the sign-convention ancestor, without claiming continuous-state or infinite-action optimality.

rows.title: The Perception-Action Loop as a Closed-Loop Active-Inference Theorem

maturity_record.invariant: Each closed-loop perception-action step is non-increasing in belief surprisal: the step's KL splits exactly into predictive and posterior parts, prediction contracts the predictive distribution (Dobrushin), and the loop invariant bounds surprisal by its initial value plus accumulated expected free energy; the loop's fixed point is the Boltzmann control posterior and equals the policy posterior of the control-as-inference view.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The loop is a finite-state kernel composition; positivity statements assume full-support likelihoods and supporting posteriors, and the contraction is the finite Dobrushin-coefficient statement, not a continuous-state or neural-implementation claim.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The strict step-wise KL decrease holds on the full-likelihood witness kernels, and at the fixed point the loop posterior coincides with the Boltzmann control posterior.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep157_loop_invariant_surprisal_bound:
theorem fep157_loop_invariant_surprisal_bound [Nonempty Policy]
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome) (belief : FiniteLaw State)
    (outcome : Outcome)
    (hEvidence : 0 < model.likelihood.predictive belief outcome)
    (support : FullSupport (withInitialState model
      (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence))) :
    -Real.log (model.likelihood.predictive belief outcome) ≤
        perceptionVFE model belief outcome hEvidence belief ∧
      perceptionVFE model belief outcome hEvidence belief =
        -Real.log (model.likelihood.predictive belief outcome) +
          finiteKL belief (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence) ∧
      expectedFreeEnergy
          (withInitialState model (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence))
          (selectedPolicy model (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence)) =
        risk (withInitialState model (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence))
            (selectedPolicy model (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence)) +
          ambiguity
            (withInitialState model (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence))
            (selectedPolicy model (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence))
qualified_declaration_statements.fep157_perception_kl_decomposition:
theorem fep157_perception_kl_decomposition
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome)
    (actual reference : FiniteLaw State)
    (hReference : ∀ s, 0 < reference s)
    (hLikelihood : ∀ s o, 0 < model.likelihood s o) :
    finiteKL actual reference =
      finiteKL (model.likelihood.predictive actual)
          (model.likelihood.predictive reference) +
        ∑ o : Outcome, model.likelihood.predictive actual o *
          finiteKL
            (filteredBelief model actual o
              (predictive_pos_of_fullLikelihood model actual hLikelihood o))
            (filteredBelief model reference o
              (predictive_pos_of_fullLikelihood model reference hLikelihood o))

theorem fep157_perception_step_kl_nonincrease
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome)
    (actual reference : FiniteLaw State)
    (hReference : ∀ s, 0 < reference s)
    (hLikelihood : ∀ s o, 0 < model.likelihood s o) :
    ∑ o : Outcome, model.likelihood.predictive actual o *
        finiteKL
          (filteredBelief model actual o
            (predictive_pos_of_fullLikelihood model actual hLikelihood o))
          (filteredBelief model reference o
            (predictive_pos_of_fullLikelihood model reference hLikelihood o)) ≤

qualified_declaration_statements.fep157_prediction_dobrushin_contraction:
theorem fep157_prediction_dobrushin_contraction [DecidableEq State]
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome) (policy : Policy)
    {coefficient : ℝ}
    (hBound : FEP.FiniteMarkovDynamics.HasDobrushinBound
      (model.transition policy) coefficient)
    (left right : FiniteLaw State) :
    FEP.FiniteMarkovDynamics.totalVariation
        ((model.transition policy).predictive left)
        ((model.transition policy).predictive right) ≤
      coefficient * FEP.FiniteMarkovDynamics.totalVariation left right

    (hEvidence : 0 < model.likelihood.predictive belief outcome) :
    perceptionVFE model belief outcome hEvidence belief =

qualified_declaration_statements.fep157_filteredBelief_eq_forwardFilter:
theorem fep157_filteredBelief_eq_forwardFilter [DecidableEq State]
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome) (belief : FiniteLaw State)
    (outcome : Outcome)
    (hEvidence : 0 < model.likelihood.predictive belief outcome) :
    filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence =
      forwardFilter belief FiniteKernel.identity model.likelihood outcome
        (identity_forwardEvidence belief outcome FiniteKernel.identity rfl
          model.likelihood hEvidence)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep157_perceptionActionStep_eq:
theorem fep157_perceptionActionStep_eq [Nonempty Policy] [DecidableEq State]
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome) (belief : FiniteLaw State)
    (outcome : Outcome)
    (hEvidence : 0 < model.likelihood.predictive belief outcome) :
    perceptionActionStep model belief outcome hEvidence =
      (model.transition (selectedPolicy model
        (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence))).predictive
        (filteredBelief model belief outcome hEvidence)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep157_perceptionActionKernel_apply:
theorem fep157_perceptionActionKernel_apply [Nonempty Policy] [DecidableEq State]
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome) (belief : FiniteLaw State)
    (hEvidence : ∀ o : Outcome, 0 < model.likelihood.predictive belief o)
    (outcome : Outcome) (state : State) :
    perceptionActionKernel model belief hEvidence outcome state =
      perceptionActionStep model belief outcome (hEvidence outcome) state
qualified_declaration_statements.fep157_posteriorKernel_joint_eq_swap:
theorem fep157_posteriorKernel_joint_eq_swap
    (model : GenerativeModel Policy State Outcome) (prior : FiniteLaw State)
    (hEvidence : ∀ o, 0 < model.likelihood.predictive prior o)
    (o : Outcome) (s : State) :
    (posteriorKernel model prior hEvidence).joint
        (model.likelihood.predictive prior) (o, s) =
      (model.likelihood.joint prior) (s, o)

rows.statement_review: Primary is a single positive-evidence outcome surprisal bound by perceptionVFE, exact VFE=surprisal+KL to its filtered belief, plus selected-policy EFE=risk+ambiguity at the filtered model. Supporting finite KL chain decomposition bounds an observation-averaged posterior KL, native DPI bounds predictive KL, and Dobrushin bounds TV under an explicit coefficient.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: There is no declared trajectory sum or theorem that each realized observation reduces surprisal/KL. The named fixed-point theorem only states that flat EFE across policies makes policyPosterior=prior; no iterated-loop fixed-point convergence is proved. Dobrushin strict contraction needs coefficient<1, not merely a supplied bound. Existing Bayesian planning/update and exact feedback specializations are real additional content, but do not establish the stronger metadata claims.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Use a full-support likelihood/prior instance to consume the exact averaged chain rule and one-step VFE gap; separately take constant policy EFE for posterior=prior.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Individual observations can increase posterior KL even when its predictive average is bounded. An identity transition admits coefficient1 and no strict TV decrease. Flat policy EFE is not proof of a dynamical fixed point.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 017 posterior/forward filter and021/071 model-derived policy planning are genuinely connected through actual operations; aggregate loop monotonicity and accumulated expected-EFE accounting require a new trajectory-level theorem, not compilation.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Each full perception-update-select-predict step bounds the stage outcome surprisal by the recognition's perception VFE with the perception KL as the exact epistemic gap and splits the selected policy's expected free energy into its certified risk-plus-ambiguity budget.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Couples normalized action-conditioned transition rows to a positive-evidence filtered finite-belief carrier so the loop's predict stage is a controlled kernel step.

touching_relations.rationale: The perception-action loop's invariant surprisal bound factors through one action-conditioned controlled-kernel step, paired with fep-065's row-normalization law, without claiming a general POMDP fixed-point theorem.

rows.title: Bayesian Model Reduction

maturity_record.invariant: Masking evidence never lowers the model evidence: the reduced model's evidence free energy dominates the full model's, the reduced posterior obeys the multiplicative Bayes-odds law with the evidence weight and reconstructs the full posterior through the evidence ratio, and the Gibbs-certificate excess over the optimizer is exactly the KL divergence to it.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The reduction statements hold for finite measure spaces with the pinned Donsker-Varadhan duality; the Gaussian log Bayes factor is stated in the pinned natural chart of the information-geometry module and is not a generic asymptotic model-selection claim.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The masked predictive is bounded by the full evidence, and the reduced posterior reconstructs the full posterior exactly through the evidence ratio.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of all ten fep-158 declarations.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep158_reduction_free_energy_monotone:
theorem fep158_reduction_free_energy_monotone (prior : FiniteLaw Parameter)
    (weight : Parameter → ℝ) (kernel : FiniteKernel Parameter Evidence)
    (data : Evidence) (hw1 : ∀ x, weight x ≤ 1)
    (hE : 0 < maskedEvidence prior weight kernel data) :
    evidenceFreeEnergy (kernel.predictive prior data) ≤
      evidenceFreeEnergy (maskedEvidence prior weight kernel data)

theorem fep158_maskedEvidence_le_predictive (prior : FiniteLaw Parameter)
    (weight : Parameter → ℝ) (kernel : FiniteKernel Parameter Evidence)
    (data : Evidence) (hw1 : ∀ x, weight x ≤ 1) :
    maskedEvidence prior weight kernel data ≤ kernel.predictive prior data
qualified_declaration_statements.fep158_maskedPrior_predictive_eq:
theorem fep158_maskedPrior_predictive_eq (prior : FiniteLaw Parameter)
    (weight : Parameter → ℝ) (kernel : FiniteKernel Parameter Evidence)
    (data : Evidence) (hw : ∀ x, 0 ≤ weight x)
    (hZ : 0 < ∑ x, weight x * prior x) :
    kernel.predictive (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) data =
      maskedEvidence prior weight kernel data / ∑ y, weight y * prior y
qualified_declaration_statements.fep158_reduction_posterior_reconstructio:
theorem fep158_reduction_posterior_reconstruction (prior : FiniteLaw Parameter)
    (weight : Parameter → ℝ) (kernel : FiniteKernel Parameter Evidence)
    (data : Evidence) (hw : ∀ x, 0 ≤ weight x)
    (hZ : 0 < ∑ x, weight x * prior x)
    (hy : 0 < kernel.predictive (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) data)
    (x : Parameter) :
    FiniteKernel.posterior (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) kernel data hy x *
        maskedEvidence prior weight kernel data =
      weight x * prior x * kernel x data
qualified_declaration_statements.fep158_reduction_posterior_odds:
theorem fep158_reduction_posterior_odds (prior : FiniteLaw Parameter)
    (weight : Parameter → ℝ) (kernel : FiniteKernel Parameter Evidence)
    (data : Evidence) (hw : ∀ x, 0 ≤ weight x)
    (hZ : 0 < ∑ x, weight x * prior x)
    (hy : 0 < kernel.predictive (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) data)
    (x y : Parameter) :
    FiniteKernel.posterior (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) kernel data hy x *
        (weight y * prior y * kernel y data) =
      FiniteKernel.posterior (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) kernel data hy y *
        (weight x * prior x * kernel x data)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep158_reduced_posterior_reconstructs:
theorem fep158_reduced_posterior_reconstructs (prior : FiniteLaw Parameter)
    (weight : Parameter → ℝ) (kernel : FiniteKernel Parameter Evidence)
    (data : Evidence) (hw : ∀ x, 0 ≤ weight x)
    (hZ : 0 < ∑ x, weight x * prior x)
    (hP : 0 < kernel.predictive prior data)
    (hE : 0 < maskedEvidence prior weight kernel data)
    (hy : 0 < kernel.predictive (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) data)
    (x : Parameter) :
    FiniteKernel.posterior (maskedPrior prior weight hw hZ) kernel data hy x =
      FiniteKernel.posterior prior kernel data hP x * weight x *
        (kernel.predictive prior data /
          maskedEvidence prior weight kernel data)

    (natural x : ℝ) :
    Real.log
        (gaussianPDFReal (family.naturalToMean natural) family.variance x /
          gaussianPDFReal 0 family.variance x) =

rows.statement_review: For weights<=1 and positive maskedEvidence, the unnormalized masked evidence is<=full predictive evidence, hence its negative log free energy is>=the full one. Normalizing the masked prior instead yields maskedEvidence/Z, a different quantity that can exceed full evidence. Posterior reweighting/reconstruction and Gibbs optimizer gap are separately proved.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: Posterior clauses require nonnegative weights, positive prior mask normalizer and positive conditioned evidence; the primary free-energy inequality itself only assumes upper weight bound plus positive masked evidence. Finite carriers are used, not arbitrary finite measure spaces. Gaussian fixed-variance log ratio and Gibbs free-energy/KL gap do not identify reduction with general DV/statistical model selection.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Uniform two-parameter prior and likelihood(.9,.1), mask(1,0): full evidence.5, masked unnormalized.45 (lower), normalized reduced-prior evidence.9 (higher). This separates the two meanings.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: No universal monotonic direction for normalized reduced-model evidence follows from mask<=1. A mask eliminating all evidence fails positivity and cannot support ordinary logarithmic posterior reconstruction.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 026 scalar log complexity and058/059 Gibbs duality are bounded neighboring facts.158 supports exact finite reweighting and specified evidence comparisons, not the reversed sentence that masking never lowers evidence.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Evidence weighting never lowers the model's evidence free energy because masked evidence never exceeds full evidence and negative log is decreasing in the evidence.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Reinterprets the finite Gibbs variational lower bound as masking monotonicity over a pointwise weight between zero and one with the exact reduced-prior renormalization.

touching_relations.rationale: Masked evidence never lowers evidence free energy, paired with fep-058's exact Gibbs lower bound on the same finiteKL and gibbsFreeEnergy carriers, without claiming a variational characterization of arbitrary model reductions.

rows.title: EFE and Entropy-Production Time-Scale Separation

maturity_record.invariant: The two-state belief information gap is bounded by the entropy-production rate scaled by the relaxation time (gain at most production/decay), the evolved gap contracts to the invariant measure no slower than the relaxation timescale, the one-slice path-space entropy production equals (1 - rho) * sigma / decay, and under the 1/eps rate scaling the evolved gain after any fixed positive action time vanishes.
maturity_record.assumption_review: All statements are for the explicit two-state continuous-time semigroup and its scaled one-parameter family; the slice-path identity is the one-slice restriction of the path-thermodynamics production, not a general path-space theorem. The ness_flow import is an orphan-adoption marker with no mathematical dependence.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The bound is attained by the stationary law for the benchmark rates, and the fast-relaxation limit exhibits the vanishing exactly.

rows.title: Helmholtz–Ao Decomposition of Nonequilibrium Steady Currents

maturity_record.invariant: On a finite state space with a full-support stationary law, every rate field decomposes exactly into a reversible part (detailed-balanced relative to the law) plus a circulation part (skew in the law-weighted sense); the stationary edge current equals twice the law-weighted circulation part, the reversible part carries no current, removing the circulation part is exactly detailed balance, the log-affinity splits into the Ao-potential drop plus the skew force, stationarity makes the node divergence of the stationary current vanish, and the directed three-cycle witness is stationary, divergence-free, and circulating.
maturity_record.assumption_review: All statements are finite-carrier algebra: the Ao potential is the pointwise -log p* mass field and is deliberately distinct from the thermodynamic Helmholtz free energy of fep-013; the continuum Fokker-Planck equation, a state-dependent diffusion matrix field, and SDE noise are not formalized. Stationarity and the probability current reuse the established FEP.ContinuousTimeMarkov generator contract.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The decomposition is unconditional for every rate field under the full-support hypothesis, and the directed three-cycle exhibits a genuine NESS whose circulation part is 1/2 at the forward edge.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of all thirteen fep-160 declarations.

rows.title: Uniqueness of the Law-Weighted Reversible/Circulation Split

maturity_record.invariant: Any competing pair S, A with W = S + A, p-weighted reversibility of S and p-weighted skewness of A coincides pointwise with the canonical symmetricPart and circulationPart of the rate field; the reversible boundary is in uniqueness form (a p-reversible field has the split (W, 0)), and on the concrete two-state datum the constraint-satisfying split is the canonical one with genuinely nonzero forward circulation 1/2 and strictly negative reverse entry -1/4.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Positivity of the finite law is the only analytic input and licenses the divisions; no stationarity hypothesis, no generator contract, and no nonnegativity claim for the circulation part enter the statements.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The t-0060 datum with weight law p = (1/3, 2/3) and rate entries 1, 5/2, 3/4, and -1 satisfies every constraint clause, its split is forced to be the canonical one, and the circulation entries 1/2 and -1/4 are computed exactly, so the uniqueness characterization is exercised on nontrivial data.
